input.strategy_title: Queue-aware GPU scheduling for distributed training workloads
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Large training jobs fail or waste capacity because pods are admitted piecemeal:
a 16-GPU job can hold 12 GPUs for hours waiting for the last 4, starving other
teams, and partially scheduled jobs die on timeout. Customers running mixed
fleets also report that jobs land on suboptimal GPU topologies (crossing NVLink
domains) with significant throughput loss. We need admission and placement that
treats a multi-node training job as one unit and uses GPU topology where it
matters.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing: no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Per-project GPU quota is enforced at admission time across training job types (PyTorchJob, RayJob). |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Users can see queue position, quota consumption, and admission state for their pending jobs in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Higher-priority workloads can preempt lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Job placement can prefer GPU-topology-aligned nodes when the cluster exposes topology information. |

## Affected Components

- Distributed Workloads
- Training Operator
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- GPU sharing/fractioning (MIG, time-slicing policy management)
- Cross-cluster or multi-cluster queueing

## Open Questions

1. Do Kueue's current gang-admission semantics (waitForPodsReady) actually
   satisfy HLR-1 for PyTorchJob and RayJob at our target scale, or do we need
   scheduler-plugin work (e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue? The answer changes
   the shape of most implementation work.
2. Topology-aware placement (HLR-5) depends on node topology discovery that is
   only Tech Preview — is it mature enough to build on this release?
3. What preemption semantics do reference customers actually need — full
   eviction with requeue, or checkpoint-aware graceful preemption? We have
   conflicting field signals and no benchmark of checkpoint overhead.

# Kueue-native gang admission for multi-node training jobs

## Description

Implements HLR-1 using Kueue's native all-or-nothing admission (waitForPodsReady),
selected when the gang-admission validation investigation confirms Kueue semantics are
sufficient at target scale. Multi-node training jobs are admitted all-or-nothing: no
partial GPU occupation while waiting for the remaining pods.

## Scope

- Enable and configure Kueue's waitForPodsReady gang-admission semantics for PyTorchJob
  and RayJob workloads (admission timeout, pods-ready conditions) per the validation
  findings.
- Tune admission timeout and requeue behavior for partially-ready jobs so they do not
  hold GPUs indefinitely (the problem statement's "12 of 16 GPUs held for hours" failure
  mode).
- Rollback path: because this replaces the existing piecemeal admission behavior, the
  all-or-nothing semantics must be revertible per-queue via configuration (feature-flag /
  rollback requirement).
- Validation at target scale reproducing the validation investigation's decision
  criterion for both job types.
- Incidental documentation updates that fall out of this change are included here as
  scope; no separate documentation work stream.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A multi-node PyTorchJob (e.g. 16-GPU class) is admitted all-or-nothing: while pending,
  it holds zero GPUs — no partial GPU occupation while waiting for remaining pods
  (HLR-1).
- The same all-or-nothing guarantee holds for RayJob workloads.
- Partially-unready jobs are evicted and requeued within the configured timeout rather
  than holding GPUs for hours.
- Admission semantics can be reverted per-queue via configuration without platform
  reinstall (rollback / feature flag).
- Scheduling of non-training workloads is unaffected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): full coverage on the Kueue-native path (applies when the gang-admission
  validation selects this outcome).

# Kueue preemption policy with full eviction and requeue

## Description

Implements HLR-4 with full-eviction semantics, selected when the preemption-semantics
investigation chooses full eviction with requeue: higher-priority workloads preempt
lower-priority ones according to an admin-defined policy; preempted workloads are fully
evicted and requeued, to be re-admitted all-or-nothing when capacity frees.

## Scope

- Configure priority-based preemption in the queueing layer per the admin-defined policy
  chosen by the preemption-semantics investigation: which workloads may preempt which,
  per queue and per project.
- Requeue semantics for evicted workloads: a preempted job returns to the queue and is
  re-admitted when capacity is available (all-or-nothing, within per-project GPU quota).
- Administrative configuration of the preemption policy — policy adjustments require no
  code changes.
- Incidental documentation updates that fall out of this change are included here as
  scope; no separate documentation work stream.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A higher-priority workload preempts a lower-priority one according to the admin-defined
  policy (HLR-4).
- A preempted workload is requeued and re-admitted when capacity is released.
- Preemption and re-admission respect the per-project GPU quota model.
- The preemption policy is admin-configurable without code changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): full coverage on the full-eviction path (applies when the
  preemption-semantics investigation selects this outcome).

# Topology-aware job placement for GPU training workloads

## Description

Implements HLR-5: job placement prefers GPU-topology-aligned nodes (e.g. within NVLink
domains rather than crossing them) when the cluster exposes topology information.
Selected when the topology-discovery maturity assessment is a go for this release.

## Scope

- Enable topology-aware placement in the queueing/scheduling layer (building on the
  Tech Preview topology-aware scheduling capability of the platform's queueing stack) so
  multi-node GPU jobs prefer topology-aligned nodes when topology information is
  available.
- Graceful degradation: when the cluster does not expose topology information, placement
  falls back to current behavior with no regression.
- Validation on topology-exposing GPU nodes demonstrating measurably better placement
  (jobs not crossing NVLink domains where an aligned placement exists).

## Acceptance Criteria

- When topology information is exposed, pending multi-node GPU jobs are placed on
  topology-aligned nodes in preference to misaligned ones (HLR-5).
- When topology information is absent, scheduling behaves as before (no regression).
- Placement preference is demonstrable on a topology-exposing cluster (aligned placement
  chosen where feasible).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2): full coverage on the proceed path (applies when the topology-discovery
  maturity assessment selects this outcome).

# Coscheduling scheduler-plugin integration for gang admission

## Description

Implements HLR-1 via scheduler-plugin work (e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue, selected
when the gang-admission validation investigation finds Kueue's native waitForPodsReady
semantics insufficient at target scale. Provides all-or-nothing admission for multi-node
training jobs, integrated with the platform's Kueue-based quota and queueing model.

## Scope

- Integrate a coscheduling scheduler plugin (or equivalent gang-scheduling mechanism) with
  the platform scheduler, coordinated with Kueue quota/admission so both training job
  types (PyTorchJob, RayJob) receive all-or-nothing semantics.
- Pod-group semantics for multi-node training jobs: a job's pods are placed as a group or
  not at all, with per-project GPU quota still enforced at admission.
- Rollback path: the plugin can be disabled per-queue or cluster-wide via configuration,
  reverting to previous scheduling behavior without reinstall (this replaces existing
  piecemeal admission behavior).
- Platform-level review of the scheduler configuration change (deploying a scheduler
  plugin is a platform-scope change beyond a single component).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Multi-node PyTorchJob and RayJob workloads are admitted all-or-nothing: no partial GPU
  occupation while waiting for remaining pods (HLR-1).
- Gang admission composes with per-project GPU quota enforcement at admission time.
- Disabling the plugin reverts to previous scheduling behavior without platform
  reinstall (rollback / feature flag).
- No regression to scheduling of non-training workloads.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): full coverage on the scheduler-plugin path (applies when the
  gang-admission validation selects this outcome).

# Checkpoint-aware graceful preemption — queueing side

## Description

Implements the queueing side of HLR-4 with checkpoint-aware graceful preemption
semantics, selected when the preemption-semantics investigation chooses graceful
semantics: when a higher-priority workload preempts a lower-priority training job, the
job is signaled to checkpoint and stopped gracefully within a bounded grace period, then
requeued and restored on re-admission.

## Scope

- Graceful preemption mechanism in the queueing layer: on preemption, notify the workload
  to checkpoint, allow a bounded grace period, then complete eviction and requeue the
  workload for re-admission.
- Admin-defined preemption policy (priority scheme, preemptability) as specified by the
  preemption-semantics investigation.
- Integration of the grace/checkpoint protocol with the per-project GPU quota model on
  re-admission.
- If the queueing layer's native hooks are insufficient for graceful preemption,
  coordinate the required upstream contribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On preemption per the admin-defined policy, a training job receives a checkpoint signal
  and a bounded grace period before eviction (HLR-4).
- The preempted job is requeued and, on re-admission, resumes from its checkpoint
  (restore is completed by the training-side checkpoint hooks).
- Checkpoint overhead stays within the bounds characterized by the preemption-semantics
  investigation's benchmark.
- The preemption policy is admin-configurable without code changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): queueing-side coverage on the graceful path (applies when the
  preemption-semantics investigation selects this outcome; training-side coverage is
  provided by the PyTorchJob checkpoint hooks in the same branch).

# PyTorchJob checkpoint hooks for graceful preemption

## Description

Implements the training side of checkpoint-aware graceful preemption for HLR-4 in the
Training Operator: PyTorchJob workloads respond to a preemption-triggered checkpoint
signal by saving state within the bounded grace period, and restore from the checkpoint
when the requeued job is re-admitted. Selected when the preemption-semantics
investigation chooses graceful semantics.

## Scope

- Checkpoint-on-signal support for PyTorchJob: on graceful-preemption notification, the
  job's workers save a checkpoint within the bounded grace period defined by the
  queueing-side graceful preemption work.
- Restore-on-restart: when the requeued job is re-admitted, training resumes from the
  latest checkpoint.
- Multi-node consistency: checkpoint and restore are correct for distributed
  (multi-node, multi-GPU) jobs.
- Coordination with the graceful-preemption protocol defined by the queueing-side work
  in the same branch (signal semantics, grace period, checkpoint location).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A preempted multi-node PyTorchJob saves a usable checkpoint within the grace period.
- On re-admission, the job restores from the checkpoint and training progresses correctly
  (no loss beyond the checkpoint interval).
- Checkpoint save and restore times are within the bounds characterized by the
  preemption-semantics investigation's benchmark.
- Jobs that do not opt into checkpointing are unaffected (graceful preemption degrades to
  plain eviction for them).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): training-side coverage on the graceful path (applies when the
  preemption-semantics investigation selects checkpoint-aware graceful semantics).

# Validate Kueue gang admission for multi-node training jobs at target scale

## Description

Resolves the strategy's first open question: whether Kueue's current all-or-nothing
admission semantics (waitForPodsReady) satisfy the all-or-nothing admission requirement
(HLR-1) for PyTorchJob and RayJob workloads at the platform's target scale, or whether
scheduler-plugin work (e.g. coscheduling) beyond Kueue is required. The strategy states
this answer "changes the shape of most implementation work", so the outcome gates the
gang-admission implementation and is recorded as a bounded two-outcome decision.

## Scope
